**2024-11-02.** Started properly at last. 1911 census on the National Archives site: house 14, Ballyragget, Co. Kilkenny. Patrick Brennan, 46, farm labourer, can read and write. Wife Bridget (née Dooley), 41. Seven children living, nine born. My grandfather Thomas is the youngest, aged 3. Saved the Form A as NAI/CEN/1911/KK/BALLY/14.

**2024-11-09.** 1901 census, same townland. Patrick is 38 here, so either he aged 8 years in 10 or someone was rounding. Classic: the 1908 old age pension made people suddenly older in 1911. Bridget 33 in 1901 and 41 in 1911, at least she's consistent.

**2024-12-14.** Griffith's Valuation, 1850. A Michael Brennan holds lot 6b in the same townland: house, small garden, 3 acres, rated at £1 15s. Probably Patrick's father, can't prove it yet.

**2025-01-18.** Parish registers on the NLI site, Ballyragget RC, microfilm P.5018. Found a baptism 12 March 1864: Patricius, son of Michael Brennan and Margarita Walsh. Sponsors John Walsh and Mary Brennan. So Patrick was born 1864, not 1865 and not 1873. One mystery down.

**2025-02-09.** DNA results back (Ancestry kit, €79 in the Black Friday sale). 87% Irish, 9% Scottish, 4% "Wales". No trace of [[Vikings in Dublin]], to the disappointment of my TY class. Top match: a likely second cousin, Morag Brennan-Kerr, in Paisley.

**2025-02-23.** Messaged Morag. Her great-grandmother Ellen Brennan left Ballyragget around 1892 to work in the Coats thread mills in Paisley. Ellen was Patrick's sister. So that's the 9% Scottish, or part of it. Links nicely to what I teach in [[Industrial revolution textiles]].

**2025-04-26.** Morag sent a photo of Ellen, about 1910, standing outside a tenement on George Street. Same jaw as my father. Had to put the phone down for a minute.

**2025-06-07.** Dead end: Bridget Dooley's parents. No baptism in Ballyragget or Freshford. Try the Ossory diocesan archive in Kilkenny (email sent to the archivist, ref OSS-GEN-2025-114).

**2025-07-19.** Plan for August: meet Morag in Paisley, then the Coats museum, then on to New Lanark. Folding it into the [[Road trip Scotland]] idea.
